alternatives.title: Dyson V15 Detect Absolute alternatives
alternatives.description: Other cordless vacuums to set beside the V15 Detect Absolute when you are comparing weight, run time, and charge time. A spec that only one of them lists stays on that card.
alternatives.subject: dyson-v15-detect

sections.heading: What the V15 page actually states
paragraphs: The V15 Detect Absolute page states 6.83 lb, up to 60 min of run time, a 4.5 hr charge time, a 0.2 gallon bin, whole-machine HEPA filtration, and 230 AW in Boost mode. Those six lines are the whole spec card. An alternative in this catalogue is another cordless vacuum whose card prints a weight, a run time, or a charge time you can put next to those lines.

Three cards do that. The PURE ONE S15 PRO page states 6.8 lbs, 40 min, and 4 hours, plus a 2500 mAh battery and a 0.47 L dust capacity. The IP3251 page states 18.47 lbs, up to 70 minutes measured at the hand vacuum in ECO mode, and a 6 hour charge, plus a 0.7 qt dust cup, full-size dimensions, and 21.6 volts. The V8 page states 5.58 lb, 40 min maximum, a 5 hr charge, a 0.14 gallon bin, and 115 AW in MAX mode.

sections.heading: Pick by the line you are matching
paragraphs: Pick the V15 Detect Absolute if the run-time line you need is up to 60 min, the suction line is 230 AW in Boost mode, or the filtration line is whole-machine HEPA. The stated weight is 6.83 lb and the charge line is 4.5 hrs. Pick it when those are the figures on the box you are about to match, not because a page on this site ranked it.

Pick the PURE ONE S15 PRO if the weight you are matching is 6.8 lbs, the run time is 40 min, and the charge line is 4 hours, or you need the 2500 mAh battery line and the 0.47 L dust capacity. The weight sits next to the V15 line. The run time is shorter than the V15 line.

Pick the IP3251 if the run-time sentence you are matching is up to 70 minutes at the hand vacuum in ECO mode, and you can accept a stated weight of 18.47 lbs and a 6 hour charge. That run-time sentence names a configuration. It is not the same sentence as “up to 60 min” on the V15 page.

Pick the V8 if the weight you are matching is 5.58 lb, the run time is 40 min maximum, and the suction line is 115 AW in MAX mode. The bin on that page is 0.14 gallon, against 0.2 gallon on the V15 page. The charge line is 5 hrs, longer than the V15 charge line. Both are Dyson pages, and the numbers are not the same.

sections.heading: Notices that name a different model
paragraphs: The V15 and V8 cards link a Health Canada notice for a FirstPower replacement battery for Dyson V6 series vacuums. That notice names V6. It does not name the V15 Detect Absolute or the V8 card’s model line. Read the model on the notice before applying it.

The IP3251 card links the 2015 CPSC notice for Shark Rotator Lift-Away vacuums, models NV650W, NV651, NV652, and NV660, and the Health Canada notice that names NV650W and NV652. IP3251 is not those model numbers. The recall block on this page is the catalogue match for each of the four cards.

alternatives.title: Levoit Core 300S-P alternatives
alternatives.description: Other air purifiers to set beside the Core 300S-P. Weigh weight and cabinet size on the small Levoit, and CADR or room size on the larger cards.
alternatives.subject: levoit-core-300s-p

sections.heading: The 300S-P card is a small cabinet
paragraphs: The Core 300S-P manual states AC 120 V, 60 Hz, 39 W, noise of 22–54.5 dB, dimensions of 8.7 × 8.7 × 14.2 in, and a weight of 7.48 lb. It does not print a CADR label or a room-size label. An alternative on this page is a purifier card that does print a room or CADR line, or the larger Levoit that prints both.

The Airmega Mighty AP-1512HH page states CADR of 233 smoke, 246 dust, and 240 pollen, room coverage of 361 ft² at 4.8 air changes per hour, dimensions of 16.8 × 18.3 × 9.6 in, a weight of 12.3 lb, and 77 W. The Core 600S-P page states 391 CFM, 13.7 lb, 12.3 x 12.3 x 23.6 in, 49 W, noise of 26–55 dB (as low as 26 dB per the maker), and a room line of 2,909 sq ft at 1 air change per hour or 606 sq ft at 4.8. The Blue Pure 211i Max page states a recommended room of 674 sq ft, 22.7 x 14.4 x 14.4 in, 16.2 lb, and sound of 23 to 53 dB.

sections.heading: Pick by cabinet weight or by a room line
paragraphs: Pick the Core 300S-P if the cabinet you are matching is 8.7 × 8.7 × 14.2 in at 7.48 lb and the power line is 39 W. The noise line is a range, 22–54.5 dB. Pick it when you do not need a CADR figure from the same page, because this card does not have one.

Pick the AP-1512HH if you need a CADR trio and a room line that names 361 ft² at 4.8 air changes per hour. The stated weight is 12.3 lb and the power line is 77 W, both higher than the 300S-P lines. The cabinet is larger in two of the three dimensions.

Pick the Core 600S-P if the figure you need is 391 CFM or the room line that names 606 sq ft at 4.8 air changes, in a 12.3 x 12.3 x 23.6 in cabinet at 13.7 lb. The noise line on that page is 26–55 dB (as low as 26 dB per the maker). The 300S-P noise line is 22–54.5 dB. Pick the 211i Max if the room figure you are matching is 674 sq ft recommended, at 16.2 lb, and you are reading a sound range of 23 to 53 dB rather than a CADR trio.

Do not add the Blueair square-foot line to the Coway square-foot line. One names a recommended room. The other names a room at 4.8 air changes per hour. The 600S-P page prints both an air-change rate and a CFM figure. Read the sentence on the page you are matching.

alternatives.title: Litter-Robot 4 alternatives
alternatives.description: The other self-cleaning litter box listed here is the PetSafe ScoopFree Crystal Plus. This page sets Whisker’s height, footprint, and cleaning interval next to PetSafe’s.
alternatives.subject: litter-robot-4

sections.heading: One other self-cleaning box is on the list
paragraphs: The Litter-Robot 4 page states 15 V DC, a height of 29.5 in, a footprint of 22 × 27 in, an entryway of 15.75 × 15.75 in, a weight of 24 lb empty, cleaning of up to 8 days before emptying the waste drawer in a 1-cat household, and suitability for up to 4 cats. That is the full card.

The other self-cleaning litter box in the catalogue is the ScoopFree Crystal Plus. Its page states up to 30 days of cleaning, 99% dust free crystal litter, dimensions of 28.2 x 20.4 x 6.6 in, an odor line, plug-in power, and single or multi-cat households. There is not a third automatic box on this list. A fountain, a feeder, or a harness is not an alternative to a litter box.

sections.heading: Pick by height, interval, or litter type
paragraphs: Pick the Litter-Robot 4 if the interval you are matching is up to 8 days before emptying the waste drawer in a 1-cat household, the household line is up to 4 cats, and the cabinet you can place is 29.5 in tall with a 22 × 27 in footprint and a 15.75 in entry. The power line is 15 V DC. The empty weight is 24 lb.

Pick the ScoopFree Crystal Plus if the cleaning line you are matching is up to 30 days, the height you can place is 6.6 in, and the litter line names crystal litter. The dimensions are 28.2 x 20.4 x 6.6 in, a lower stated height and a wider stated length than the Litter-Robot footprint. The power line says plug-in. The household line says single or multi-cat households, without a cat-count cap on that card.

The two cleaning lines are not the same chore. One names days before you empty a waste drawer for one cat. The other names days of cleaning and pairs that with a crystal-litter line. A longer stated interval is the ScoopFree line. A stated cat cap of 4 is the Litter-Robot line. The odor sentence lives only on the ScoopFree card. Read it there instead of treating it as a shared row.

The recall block is the catalogue match for each box. Neither card is a US or Canadian recall match on the check date printed below. Confirm the model name on the box against the name on the card before you buy.

alternatives.title: Best Roomba Combo j9+ alternatives
alternatives.description: Robots to consider beside the Roomba Combo j9+. Qrevo S, X10 Pro Omni, and Shark AV2501S are the other choices.
alternatives.subject: irobot-roomba-combo-j9-plus

sections.heading: What the Combo j9+ card states
paragraphs: The Combo j9+ page states a robot weight of 8.9 lb, robot dimensions of 3.4 x 13.7 x 13.7 in, a battery line of Lithium-ion, dock dimensions of 15.8 in W x 16.4 in D x 16.3 in H, and a dock weight of 21.9 lb. The model string on that page is C975020. An alternative here is another robot vacuum already on the cleaning list, with its own maker lines beside those five.

The Qrevo S page states suction of 7,000 Pa, robot dimensions of 13.78 x 13.9 x 3.80 in, dock dimensions of 13.38 x 19.17 x 20.51 in, mop speed of 200 RPM, a battery of 14.4 V/5200 mAh lithium-ion, and a charge time of Approx. 4 hours. The X10 Pro Omni page states suction of 8,000 Pa, a run time of 173 min vacuum, or 136 min vacuum and mop, on standard, robot dimensions of 327 mm x 353 mm x 113.5 mm, a robot weight of 4,560 g, and a dustbin of 330 ml. The AV2501S page states a weight of 14.77 lbs, a cleaning path of 5.7 in, dimensions of 15.35 in L x 12.01 in W x 17.72 in H, a dust cup of 0.1 qt, voltage of 120 volts, and wattage of 650 watts.

sections.heading: Pick by the line you can place
paragraphs: Pick the Combo j9+ if the listing is C975020 and you are matching a robot of 8.9 lb at 3.4 x 13.7 x 13.7 in, plus a dock of 15.8 in W x 16.4 in D x 16.3 in H that weighs 21.9 lb. The battery line says lithium-ion. It does not state a milliamp hour or a run time. A listing that says Roomba, or robot vacuum, still has to show C975020 if this is the card you mean.

Pick the Qrevo S if the suction line you are matching is 7,000 Pa, the mop line is 200 RPM, and the charge line is Approx. 4 hours. The dock on that page is 13.38 x 19.17 x 20.51 in. The Combo j9+ dock height line is 16.3 in H. Those are different sentences. The Qrevo battery line names 14.4 V/5200 mAh lithium-ion. This page does not convert that into the Combo j9+ battery sentence.

Pick the X10 Pro Omni if the suction line is 8,000 Pa or the run-time sentence is 173 min vacuum, or 136 min vacuum and mop, on standard. The robot weight is 4,560 g and the dimensions are 327 mm x 353 mm x 113.5 mm. The dustbin line is 330 ml. Grams, millimetres, and millilitres are the units on that card. The Combo j9+ card uses pounds and inches. Leave each figure in the units printed with it.

Pick the AV2501S if you are matching 14.77 lbs, a cleaning path of 5.7 in, and a dust cup of 0.1 qt. The dimension line is 15.35 in L x 12.01 in W x 17.72 in H. The electrical lines are 120 volts and 650 watts. That card does not print a pascal figure. A watt line is not a pascal line, and this page does not treat them as the same claim.

sections.heading: Robot weight and dock weight stay apart
paragraphs: The Combo j9+ card prints the robot and the dock as separate weights, 8.9 lb and 21.9 lb. This page does not add them into one figure. The Qrevo S card prints robot dimensions and dock dimensions and does not print a robot weight. The X10 card prints a robot weight in grams and a dustbin in millilitres. The AV2501S card prints one weight, 14.77 lbs, on a dimension line that is taller than the Combo j9+ robot height of 3.4 in. Read the sentence that names the part you are placing.

Qrevo S, X10 Pro Omni, and AV2501S are different model strings from C975020. The recall block below is the catalogue match for each of the four cards. Open the model page for the feed link, and search the model on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts before you buy. A brand name in a listing title is not the model string on the card.

alternatives.title: Best Sony WH-1000XM5 alternatives
alternatives.description: Headphones to consider beside the WH-1000XM5. QuietComfort Ultra, AirPods Pro 3, and OpenRun Pro 2 have different battery lives.
alternatives.subject: sony-wh-1000xm5

sections.heading: What the XM5 card states
paragraphs: The Sony card states model WH-1000XM5, battery life of Max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on, max. 40 hours with it off, noise cancelling described as 2 processors control 8 microphones, connection of Multipoint, a weight of Approx. 8.82 oz, and a charge time of Approx. 3.5 hours. An alternative on this page is another personal-tech card with a battery or play-time line you can read next to those sentences. Two of them are not over-ear headband headphones.

The QuietComfort Ultra page states battery of Up to 24 hours, modes of Quiet, Aware, and Immersion, Bluetooth of Multipoint, two devices, audio of Bose Immersive Audio, a weight of 0.56 lb, and a charge time of 3 hours. The AirPods Pro 3 page states listening of Up to 8 hours with Active Noise Cancellation, transparency of Up to 10 hours with the Hearing Aid feature, a sensor line of Heart rate, a hearing line of Hearing Aid feature, play time of Up to 8 hours with Active Noise Cancellation, and a rating of IP57. The OpenRun Pro 2 page states play time of Up to 12 hours, a quick-charge line of 5 minutes for about 150 minutes at 75% volume, drivers of Dual, and a rating of IP55.

sections.heading: Pick the battery sentence, then the form
paragraphs: Pick the WH-1000XM5 if the listing shows that model and you are matching Max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on, max. 40 hours with it off, a weight of Approx. 8.82 oz, and a charge time of Approx. 3.5 hours. The microphone sentence is 2 processors control 8 microphones. The connection line says multipoint. A listing that says Sony headphones, or 1000X, still has to show WH-1000XM5 if this is the card.

Pick the QuietComfort Ultra if you are matching Up to 24 hours, a charge time of 3 hours, and modes named Quiet, Aware, and Immersion. The weight on that page is 0.56 lb. The Sony weight is in ounces. This page does not convert ounces into pounds. A shorter stated charge time is the Bose line. A longer stated playback line with noise cancelling on is the Sony line. Multipoint is on both cards, and the Bose card adds two devices.

Pick the AirPods Pro 3 if you are matching in-ear listening of Up to 8 hours with Active Noise Cancellation, the same Up to 8 hours with Active Noise Cancellation play-time line, a rating of IP57, and the hearing line that says Hearing Aid feature. The transparency line is Up to 10 hours with the Hearing Aid feature. The sensor line says Heart rate. Those sentences are not on the WH-1000XM5 card. Eight hours and thirty hours are different playback lines.

Pick the OpenRun Pro 2 if you are matching open-ear play time of Up to 12 hours, a rating of IP55, and the quick-charge sentence 5 minutes for about 150 minutes at 75% volume. The driver line says Dual. That card is not a headband headphone and it is not an in-ear bud. A 12 hour line sits between the AirPods play-time line and the Sony noise-cancelling line, and it is still its own sentence.

sections.heading: Do not collapse the form factor
paragraphs: WH-1000XM5 and QuietComfort Ultra are over-ear cards with weight and charge lines. AirPods Pro 3 is an in-ear card with a listening line, a hearing line, and IP57. OpenRun Pro 2 is an open-ear card with IP55 and a quick-charge line. A shared idea of battery life is not a shared label. Read the hours on the page for the form you are actually buying.

The recall block is the catalogue match for each of the four cards. Confirm the model printed on the box. WH-1000XM5, QuietComfort Ultra, AirPods Pro 3, and OpenRun Pro 2 are four model strings. The comparison page for Sony and Bose repeats only the labels both of those cards share.

worth.title: Is the Litter-Robot 4 worth it?
worth.description: The Litter-Robot 4 suits a household that can spare 29.5 in of height and a 22 × 27 in footprint, and that wants up to 8 days before emptying the waste drawer for one cat, with a stated cap of 4 cats. If the box has to be much shorter, or you want a longer cleaning interval, weigh the ScoopFree Crystal Plus.
worth.subject: litter-robot-4

sections.heading: The question is which lines fit the room
paragraphs: On this page, worth it means the maker’s lines describe the space and the chore you have. It is not a price verdict. The Litter-Robot 4 page states a height of 29.5 in, a footprint of 22 × 27 in, an entryway of 15.75 × 15.75 in, an empty weight of 24 lb, power of 15 V DC, up to 8 days before emptying the waste drawer in a 1-cat household, and up to 4 cats.

If the floor opening is smaller than 22 × 27 in, or the vertical space is under 29.5 in, the cabinet line does not fit, whatever else the page says. If the household is one cat and the chore you are matching is the waste-drawer interval, the line to read is up to 8 days. If the household line you need is a stated cap, the page says up to 4 cats.

sections.heading: Pick it, or pick the lower box
paragraphs: Pick the Litter-Robot 4 if all of these are true on the page you are reading: the height is acceptable at 29.5 in, the footprint fits at 22 × 27 in, the entry is 15.75 in square, and the interval you want is the waste-drawer line for one cat. The power supply line is 15 V DC, so the card is not describing a battery tray.

Pick the ScoopFree Crystal Plus instead if the height you can give the box is 6.6 in, the cleaning line you want is up to 30 days, and the litter line you want names crystal litter. That page also states 28.2 x 20.4 x 6.6 in, plug-in power, and single or multi-cat households. It does not state an empty weight or a cat-count cap. A short cabinet and a long interval are the ScoopFree lines. A tall cabinet and an 8-day drawer line are the Litter-Robot lines.

The two pages do not share a label, so there is no single table row that decides this. Read the height first, then the interval, then the household sentence. The recall lines below are the catalogue match. Open the model page for the feed link.

worth.title: Is the Vitamix E310 worth it?
worth.description: The E310 suits someone who wants a blender with a 2 HP motor, a 48 oz container, and a 5-year full warranty, if a cabinet of 9 × 8 × 18 in and a weight of 10.5 lb will fit. The Cuisinart food processor on the kitchen list is a different tool, and it has a US recall.
worth.subject: vitamix-e310

sections.heading: Five lines on the E310 card
paragraphs: The Vitamix E310 page states a 2 HP motor, a 48 oz container, dimensions of 9 × 8 × 18 in, a weight of 10.5 lb, and a 5-year full warranty. Worth it means those lines describe the counter and the jar you want. A 2 HP line is a motor claim from Vitamix. An 18 in height is the cabinet line to check against the space under a cabinet.

The nearest motor appliance on the kitchen list that shares a motor label and a dimensions label is the Cuisinart Custom 14-Cup DFP-14BCNY. That page states a 14 cup bowl, a 720 W motor, dimensions of 11 in L x 7.9 in W x 14.8 in H, a 5-year motor warranty, and a 3-year limited warranty on the whole unit. A blender jar in ounces and a food-processor bowl in cups are different tools. The shared labels are only a reason to notice the difference, not a reason to treat them as the same machine.

sections.heading: Pick the blender line or stop for the recall
paragraphs: Pick the E310 if you are matching a blender, the motor line you want is 2 HP, the jar line is 48 oz, and an 18 in height at 10.5 lb fits the counter. The warranty line on that page is a 5-year full warranty. Pick it for those sentences.

Do not pick the DFP-14BCNY as a second E310. Pick that card only if you are matching a 14 cup food processor with a 720 W motor line and a lower stated height of 14.8 in. The US catalogue line for DFP-14BCNY is a recall match. The notice linked from that model page is the Conair Cuisinart food-processor recall. Read the model numbers on the notice before buying that processor. The Canadian line on the card is a separate check.
A wattage and a horsepower line are not the same unit. This page does not convert 2 HP into watts or 720 W into horsepower. The recall block below repeats the catalogue status for each model.

worth.title: Is the Sony WH-1000XM5 worth it?
worth.description: The WH-1000XM5 suits someone who wants over-ear headphones with max. 30 hours of battery with noise cancelling on, or max. 40 hours with it off, at about 8.82 oz, and can wait about 3.5 hours to charge. Weigh the Bose QuietComfort Ultra if you want a 3 hour charge and up to 24 hours of battery.
worth.subject: sony-wh-1000xm5

sections.heading: The lines that answer a headphone match
paragraphs: The Sony specifications page states a weight of about 8.82 oz, a charge time of about 3.5 hours, and battery life of max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on or max. 40 hours with it off. The product page also states the model WH-1000XM5, that 2 processors control 8 microphones, and multipoint. Worth it means you are buying that model and those battery and weight lines are the ones you meant to match.

The QuietComfort Ultra specifications table states up to 24 hours, a weight of 0.56 lb, and a 3 hour charge, plus Quiet, Aware, and Immersion modes, multipoint for two devices, and Bose Immersive Audio. The weight units differ: ounces on the Sony page, pounds on the Bose page. This page does not convert them.

sections.heading: Pick the longer battery line or the shorter charge line
paragraphs: Pick the WH-1000XM5 if the battery line you are matching is max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on, or max. 40 hours with it off, and the weight line you are matching is about 8.82 oz. The charge line that goes with that page is about 3.5 hours. Pick it if the microphone sentence, 2 processors and 8 microphones, is the noise-cancelling description you meant.

Pick the QuietComfort Ultra if the battery line you are matching is up to 24 hours, the charge line is 3 hours, and the mode line names Quiet, Aware, and Immersion. A shorter stated charge time is the Bose line. A longer stated playback line with noise cancelling on is the Sony line. Multipoint appears on both cards, with the Bose card adding “two devices.”

Neither card is a US or Canadian recall match on the catalogue date below. Confirm WH-1000XM5 on the box if that is the model you are buying. The Bose card is a different model with its own battery sentence. The comparison page for this pair repeats only the labels both cards share, which are battery, weight, and charge time, and it leaves the microphone line and the mode line on the separate cards.

worth.title: Is the Zojirushi rice cooker worth it?
worth.description: The NS-ZCC10 suits someone who wants a rice cooker for up to 5.5 cups and has 8-1/8 inches of height for it. An Instant Pot Duo Plus can cook rice too, but it is a 6 quart multi-cooker, not a dedicated rice pot.
worth.subject: zojirushi-ns-zcc10

sections.heading: The question is which lines fit the pot
paragraphs: On this page, worth it means the maker’s lines describe the rice pot you are trying to place. It is not a price verdict. The NS-ZCC10 page states a capacity of Up to 5.5 cups / 1.0 liter, dimensions of 10-1/8 x 13 x 8-1/8 inches, electrical of 120 volts / 680 watts, and origin of Made in Japan. Those four lines are the card. A listing that says Zojirushi, or rice cooker, still has to show NS-ZCC10 if these are the lines you mean.

This catalogue has no Tiger rice cooker card, so there is no Tiger capacity line to put beside the 5.5 cup line. The kitchen card that names rice is the Duo Plus. Its function list is Pressure cook, slow cook, sauté, sous vide, steam, sterilize, keep warm, rice, and yogurt. It also states a capacity of 6 quart, power of 1,000 W, 120 V, 60 Hz, cleanup of Dishwasher-safe, and dimensions of 12.2 L x 13.4 W x 12.9 H in. Rice is one name in that function list. It is not a dedicated rice-cooker capacity in cups.

sections.heading: Pick the cup line or the function list
paragraphs: Pick the NS-ZCC10 if you are matching a rice cooker, the capacity line is Up to 5.5 cups / 1.0 liter, the cabinet is 10-1/8 x 13 x 8-1/8 inches, and the electrical line is 120 volts / 680 watts. The origin line says Made in Japan. The height in that dimension line is 8-1/8 inches. That is the vertical figure to hold against the space under a cabinet.

Pick the Duo Plus if you are matching a 6 quart multi-cooker whose function list includes rice among pressure cook, slow cook, sauté, and the other names on that page, at 1,000 W, 120 V, 60 Hz. The dimension line is 12.2 L x 13.4 W x 12.9 H in. A 6 quart bowl and a 5.5 cup rice line are not the same measure. This page does not convert cups into quarts or 680 watts into 1,000 watts.

The two cleanup stories differ as well. The Duo Plus card says Dishwasher-safe. The NS-ZCC10 card does not print a cleanup line. Do not borrow the dishwasher sentence for the rice cooker. Read the electrical line on the cooker you are plugging in: 120 volts / 680 watts on the Zojirushi page, and 1,000 W, 120 V, 60 Hz on the Duo Plus page.

sections.heading: What a listing still has to show
paragraphs: A season name or a price on a listing is not the model string. For the rice cooker, the string to match is NS-ZCC10, with the 5.5 cup / 1.0 liter capacity and the 10-1/8 x 13 x 8-1/8 inch cabinet. For the multi-cooker, match the Duo Plus function list and the 6 quart line. The recall block below is the catalogue match for each card. Official Instant Pot notices on the recall desk name other Instant Pot models. Open that explainer and read the model list before treating a family name as this Duo Plus card.

If the cabinet under your shelf is shorter than 8-1/8 inches, the NS-ZCC10 dimension line does not fit, whatever else the page says. If you need pressure cook in the same function list as rice, that sentence is on the Duo Plus card, not on the Zojirushi card. Pick the card whose sentence you can point to on the maker page.

worth.title: Is the Breville Barista Express worth it?
worth.description: The Barista Express suits someone who wants one machine that grinds the beans and pulls the espresso. The Baratza Encore ESP is a separate grinder, and the Fellow Stagg EKG is a kettle with temperature control.
worth.subject: breville-bes870xl

sections.heading: The Barista Express lines
paragraphs: Worth it means the BES870XL sentences describe the espresso setup you are placing on the counter. It is not a price verdict, and it is not a claim about when a listing changes. The Breville page states model BES870XL, a grinder of Integrated conical burr grinder with 16 grind settings, a portafilter of 54 mm stainless steel, a dose of 18 g, and extraction of Low-pressure pre-infusion, then 9 bar, from a 15 bar pump.

Two other coffee cards sit on the kitchen list, and neither is a second espresso machine. The Encore ESP page states burrs of 40 mm conical steel, a hopper of 300 g, power of 70 W, 100-120 V, settings of 1-20 espresso, 21-40 filter, and a warranty of 1 year. The Stagg EKG page states power of 1200 W, temperature of To-the-degree control, a hold line of Keeps the set temperature while you pour, and listed capacities of 0.9 L (30 oz) and 1.5 L (50 oz) sizes on the maker page. A kettle and a separate grinder are different tools from an integrated machine.

sections.heading: Pick the integrated machine, the grinder, or the kettle
paragraphs: Pick the BES870XL if the listing shows that model and you are matching an integrated conical burr grinder with 16 grind settings, a 54 mm stainless steel portafilter, an 18 g dose, and extraction that the page describes as low-pressure pre-infusion, then 9 bar, from a 15 bar pump. Those five lines are the card. A listing that says Breville, or Barista, still has to show BES870XL if this is the machine.

Pick the Encore ESP if you are matching a separate grinder: 40 mm conical steel, a hopper of 300 g, and settings of 1-20 espresso, 21-40 filter. The power line is 70 W, 100-120 V. The warranty line is 1 year. The BES870XL card does not print a hopper weight or a 40 mm burr. Sixteen grind settings on the Breville page and the 1-20 espresso range on the Baratza page are different sentences.

Pick the Stagg EKG if you are matching a kettle, not an espresso machine. The power line is 1200 W. The temperature line says To-the-degree control. The hold line says it keeps the set temperature while you pour. The capacity line names 0.9 L (30 oz) and 1.5 L (50 oz) sizes on the maker page. A 1200 W kettle line is not the extraction line on the BES870XL card. This page does not turn one into the other.

sections.heading: What to read on the listing
paragraphs: Match the model string first. BES870XL is the espresso machine. The Encore ESP is the grinder with 40 mm conical steel burrs. The Stagg EKG is the kettle. A listing that bundles a different model number is a different card. The recall block below is the catalogue match for each of the three. None of these three cards is a stand mixer or a rice cooker.

If you want the dose and the portafilter in one machine, the lines to read are 18 g and 54 mm stainless steel on the BES870XL page, with the extraction sentence that names 9 bar from a 15 bar pump. If you want a grinder you can use for filter as well as espresso, the settings line to read is on the Encore ESP page: 1-20 espresso, 21-40 filter. If you want water at a set temperature, that sentence is on the Stagg EKG page.

season.title: Dyson V15 Detect: what to know before you buy
season.description: The V15 Detect Absolute maker lines for weight, run time, charge time, bin, filtration, and suction, next to the V8, S15 PRO, and IP3251 cards, with the dated recall check.
season.subject: dyson-v15-detect

sections.heading: Match the model name before the accessory list
paragraphs: The V15 Detect Absolute page states 6.83 lb, up to 60 min of run time, a 4.5 hr charge time, a 0.2 gallon bin, whole-machine HEPA filtration, and 230 AW in Boost mode. A listing that says Detect, or V15, or Absolute, still has to match this model line. The V8 card in the same catalogue is a different vacuum: 5.58 lb, 40 min maximum, a 5 hr charge, a 0.14 gallon bin, and 115 AW in MAX mode.

Two other cordless cards sit next to it. The PURE ONE S15 PRO page states 6.8 lbs, 40 min, a 4 hour charge, a 2500 mAh battery, and a 0.47 L dust capacity. The IP3251 page states 18.47 lbs, up to 70 minutes measured at the hand vacuum in ECO mode, a 6 hour charge, a 0.7 qt dust cup, dimensions of 10.24 in L x 18.5 in W x 46.46 in H, and 21.6 volts.

sections.heading: Pick the card whose sentence is on the listing
paragraphs: Pick the V15 Detect Absolute if the listing names that model and you are matching up to 60 min, 230 AW in Boost mode, and whole-machine HEPA filtration. The weight line to confirm is 6.83 lb. The charge line is 4.5 hrs. The bin line is 0.2 gallon.

Pick the V8 if the listing is the V8 and you are matching 5.58 lb, 40 min maximum, and 115 AW in MAX mode. Pick the PURE ONE S15 PRO if you are matching 6.8 lbs, 40 min, and a 4 hour charge, or you need the 2500 mAh line. Pick the IP3251 if the sentence you are matching is up to 70 minutes at the hand vacuum in ECO mode, and the stated weight of 18.47 lbs is acceptable.

A Health Canada notice linked from the V15 and V8 cards names a FirstPower replacement battery for Dyson V6 series vacuums. It names V6, not the V15 Detect Absolute. The IP3251 card links the 2015 Rotator notice, which names NV650W, NV651, NV652, and NV660 on the CPSC page and NV650W and NV652 on the Health Canada page. IP3251 is not those numbers. Read the model on the notice, then read the model on the box.

season.title: Litter-Robot 4: check the cabinet lines before you buy
season.description: Height, footprint, entry, empty weight, drawer interval, and cat cap as the Whisker page states them, next to the ScoopFree Crystal Plus lines, with the dated recall check.
season.subject: litter-robot-4

sections.heading: The cabinet is the first match
paragraphs: The Litter-Robot 4 page states 15 V DC, a height of 29.5 in, a footprint of 22 × 27 in, an entryway of 15.75 × 15.75 in, a weight of 24 lb empty, up to 8 days before emptying the waste drawer in a 1-cat household, and up to 4 cats. If the opening in the room is shorter than 29.5 in or narrower than that footprint, the rest of the card does not make the unit fit.

The other self-cleaning box on the list is the ScoopFree Crystal Plus. Its page states up to 30 days of cleaning, crystal litter, dimensions of 28.2 x 20.4 x 6.6 in, plug-in power, and single or multi-cat households. The height line is 6.6 in. That is a different cabinet.

sections.heading: Pick by height and by the interval sentence
paragraphs: Pick the Litter-Robot 4 if the listing is that model and the room accepts 29.5 in of height, a 22 × 27 in footprint, and a 15.75 in entry, and the chore you are matching is up to 8 days before emptying the waste drawer for one cat. The household line is up to 4 cats. The power line is 15 V DC. The empty weight is 24 lb.

Pick the ScoopFree Crystal Plus if the listing is that box and you are matching a 6.6 in height, up to 30 days of cleaning, and a crystal-litter line. The length on that page is 28.2 in, wider than the Litter-Robot footprint’s 27 in side, and much lower. The household line does not state a cat-count cap.

The two interval sentences are not interchangeable. One names a waste drawer and a one-cat household. The other names days of cleaning and pairs it with crystal litter. The recall block is the catalogue match for each box on the check date. Confirm the name on the carton against the name on the card.

season.title: Instant Pot Duo Plus: check the 6-quart lines before you buy
season.description: Capacity, functions, power, and dimensions as the Duo Plus page states them, next to the Foodi 10-in-1 lines, with the older Instant Pot and Foodi notices that name other models.
season.subject: instant-pot-duo-plus

sections.heading: Duo Plus is a specific function list
paragraphs: The Duo Plus page states pressure cook, slow cook, sauté, sous vide, steam, sterilize, keep warm, rice, and yogurt, a 6 quart volume, 1,000 W at 120 V and 60 Hz, dishwasher-safe cleanup, and dimensions of 12.2 L x 13.4 W x 12.9 H in. A listing that says Instant Pot, or 6 quart, or Duo, still has to match this function list and this wattage if this is the card you mean.

The Foodi 10-in-1 page states Air Fry, Whole Roast, Air Roast, Bake, Dehydrate, Pizza, Broil, Toast, Bagel, and Reheat, a capacity line for a 5 lb chicken and a sheet pan of vegetables, two 12 in pizzas, or a 12 lb turkey, 1,800 W, and dimensions of 62.2 × 50.6 × 42.49 cm. Those are different functions and a higher stated wattage. The model line on that card is DT201C.

sections.heading: Pick the function list, then read the other model numbers
paragraphs: Pick the Duo Plus if the listing is the 6 quart Duo Plus and you are matching pressure cook among the functions, 1,000 W, and the inch dimensions above. Pick the Foodi 10-in-1 if the listing is the DT201C and you are matching the air-fry and roast function list, 1,800 W, and the centimetre dimensions.

Official Instant Pot notices on the recall desk name Smart, Smart-60, and Gem 65. They do not name Duo Plus. The Foodi OP300-series notice names pressure-cooker model numbers in the OP300 series, not DT201C and not the FN101 Crispi. Open those explainers and read the model list before treating a family name as this card.

The recall block below is the catalogue match for the Duo Plus and for the Foodi 10-in-1. A family name on a seasonal listing is not the model number. The wattage row is 1,000 W on the Duo Plus page and 1,800 W on the Foodi page, and the dimension row uses inches on one page and centimetres on the other.

season.title: Sony WH-1000XM5: check the battery line before you buy
season.description: Weight, charge time, and battery life as the Sony specifications page states them for the WH-1000XM5, next to the QuietComfort Ultra lines, with the dated recall check.
season.subject: sony-wh-1000xm5

sections.heading: The model string is WH-1000XM5
paragraphs: The Sony card states model WH-1000XM5, battery life of max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on or max. 40 hours with it off, a weight of about 8.82 oz, a charge time of about 3.5 hours, multipoint, and that 2 processors control 8 microphones. A listing that says Sony headphones, or 1000X, still has to show WH-1000XM5 if this is the card you are matching.

The QuietComfort Ultra page states up to 24 hours, 0.56 lb, a 3 hour charge, Quiet, Aware, and Immersion modes, multipoint for two devices, and Bose Immersive Audio. The weight units are ounces on the Sony page and pounds on the Bose page. This page does not convert them.

sections.heading: Pick the battery sentence you meant
paragraphs: Pick the WH-1000XM5 if the listing shows that model and you are matching max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on, or max. 40 hours with it off, at about 8.82 oz, with a charge line of about 3.5 hours. The microphone sentence is 2 processors and 8 microphones.

Pick the QuietComfort Ultra if the listing is that Bose model and you are matching up to 24 hours, a 3 hour charge, and the mode names Quiet, Aware, and Immersion. A shorter stated charge time is the Bose line. A longer stated playback line with noise cancelling on is the Sony line.

Neither card is a recall match in the catalogue block below. Confirm the model printed on the earcup or the box, not only the brand in the title of the listing. Multipoint is on both cards. The Sony card states the microphone arrangement, 2 processors and 8 microphones, and the Bose card states the mode names. Those lines stay on their own cards because the other page does not use the same label. The charge lines are about 3.5 hours on the Sony page and 3 hours on the Bose page. Read both charge lines on the maker pages.

season.title: KitchenAid Artisan: check the 5-quart lines before you buy
season.description: Capacity, speeds, bowl, and model KSM150PSER as the KitchenAid page states them for the Artisan tilt-head, with the dated recall check. The catalogue has no second stand mixer.
season.subject: kitchenaid-artisan

sections.heading: KSM150PSER is the model line
paragraphs: The Artisan page states a 5 quart capacity, 10 speeds, a 5 quart stainless steel dishwasher-safe bowl, more than 10 optional hub-powered attachments sold separately, and model KSM150PSER. A listing that says KitchenAid, or Artisan, or 5 quart, still has to show KSM150PSER if this is the mixer you mean. Bowl size and a tilt-head description on a different model number are a different card, and this catalogue does not have a second stand mixer.

The Cuisinart DFP-14BCNY card is a food processor, not a mixer. It states a 14 cup bowl, a 720 W motor, dimensions of 11 in L x 7.9 in W x 14.8 in H, a 5-year motor warranty, and a 3-year limited warranty on the whole unit. It shares a kitchen counter with the Artisan. It does not share a job.

sections.heading: Pick the mixer line, and stop on the processor recall
paragraphs: Pick the Artisan if the listing is KSM150PSER and you are matching a 5 quart bowl, 10 speeds, and the attachment sentence that says more than 10 optional hub-powered attachments are sold separately. The match is those lines. There is no second mixer card here to pick instead.

Do not pick the DFP-14BCNY as the mixer. Pick that card only if you are matching a 14 cup food processor and a 720 W motor line. The US catalogue line for that processor is a recall match. The notice on the model page is the Conair Cuisinart food-processor recall. Read the model numbers there before buying the processor.

The recall block below repeats the catalogue status for the Artisan and for the processor. Confirm KSM150PSER on the mixer base if the Artisan is the one in the cart. The bowl line says 5 quart stainless steel and dishwasher-safe. The attachment line says the hub-powered tools are sold separately, so a listing that bundles a different model number is not this card.

season.title: Coway Airmega Mighty AP-1512HH: check the CADR lines before you buy
season.description: CADR, room coverage, cabinet, weight, and power as the Coway page states them for the AP-1512HH, next to the Core 300S-P, Core 600S-P, and 211i Max cards, with the dated recall check.
season.subject: coway-ap-1512hh

sections.heading: AP-1512HH is the model with this CADR trio
paragraphs: The Airmega Mighty page states CADR of 233 smoke, 246 dust, and 240 pollen, room coverage of 361 ft² at 4.8 air changes per hour, dimensions of 16.8 × 18.3 × 9.6 in, a weight of 12.3 lb, and 77 W. A listing that says Coway, or Airmega, or Mighty, still has to show AP-1512HH if these are the lines you are matching. The Airmega 250 is a different card, with its own CADR trio and a different cabinet.

The Core 300S-P manual states 7.48 lb, 8.7 × 8.7 × 14.2 in, and 39 W, with noise of 22–54.5 dB, and no CADR label. The Core 600S-P page states 391 CFM, 13.7 lb, and a room line of 606 sq ft at 4.8 air changes or 2,909 sq ft at 1. The 211i Max page states a recommended room of 674 sq ft, 16.2 lb, and 22.7 x 14.4 x 14.4 in.

sections.heading: Pick the CADR trio or a different room sentence
paragraphs: Pick the AP-1512HH if the listing shows that model and you are matching smoke 233, dust 246, pollen 240, and 361 ft² at 4.8 air changes per hour, at 12.3 lb and 77 W. The cabinet line is 16.8 × 18.3 × 9.6 in.

Pick the Core 300S-P if you are matching the smaller cabinet, 7.48 lb and 39 W, and you do not need a CADR figure from the same page. Pick the Core 600S-P if you are matching 391 CFM and the 606 sq ft line at 4.8 air changes. Pick the 211i Max if you are matching the 674 sq ft recommended line and 16.2 lb. Those room sentences are not the same kind of sentence as the AP-1512HH coverage line.

The recall block is the catalogue match for each purifier. Confirm AP-1512HH on the rating label if that is the Mighty you are buying. The 300S-P noise line is 22–54.5 dB, and the 600S-P noise line is 26–55 dB (as low as 26 dB per the maker).

season.title: Ninja Creami Black Friday: what to know before you buy
season.description: The NC301 is an ice cream maker with seven programs and two 16 oz pints in the box. Confirm that model, and do not treat a Ninja oven as the same machine.
season.subject: ninja-creami-nc301

sections.heading: NC301 is the model string
paragraphs: The CREAMi card states model NC301, programs of 7 preset programs, pints of Two 16 oz pints included, care of Containers, lids, and paddle are dishwasher safe, and a warranty of One year limited. A listing title can add a season name and still be a different machine. The string to match for this card is NC301. The box line to match is two 16 oz pints included, with containers, lids, and paddle described as dishwasher safe.

The other Ninja card on this page is the Foodi 10-in-1. It states power of 1,800 W, functions of Air Fry, Whole Roast, Air Roast, Bake, Dehydrate, Pizza, Broil, Toast, Bagel, and Reheat, a capacity line of Fits a 5 lb chicken and a sheet pan of vegetables, two 12 in pizzas, or a 12 lb turkey, dimensions of 62.2 × 50.6 × 42.49 cm, and a warranty of 1 year limited. Air Fry is one name in that function list. It is an oven card, not an ice cream maker. The NC301 card does not print an air-fry function or a wattage.

sections.heading: Pick the pint line or the oven function list
paragraphs: Pick the NC301 if the listing shows NC301 and you are matching 7 preset programs, two 16 oz pints included, and a one year limited warranty. The care line says the containers, lids, and paddle are dishwasher safe. Confirm those words on the listing and on the maker page. A different pint size, or a different program count, is a different model string.

Pick the Foodi 10-in-1 if the listing is that oven and you are matching Air Fry, Whole Roast, Air Roast, Bake, Dehydrate, Pizza, Broil, Toast, Bagel, and Reheat, at 1,800 W. The capacity sentence is Fits a 5 lb chicken and a sheet pan of vegetables, two 12 in pizzas, or a 12 lb turkey. The dimensions are 62.2 × 50.6 × 42.49 cm. Do not pick the oven because the word Ninja appears on an ice cream listing. Do not pick the CREAMi because an oven listing says Air Fry.

The comparison page for NC301 and the Deluxe NC501 is the page that lines those two ice cream makers up. This page does not copy the NC501 figures. Open that comparison and the Ninja page it cites if the listing says Deluxe, XL, or NC501. NC301 remains the 7 program card with two 16 oz pints. The Foodi OP300 notice is a pressure-cooker lid notice. It names OP300-series model numbers, not NC301. The air fryer recall list links that notice and says what it covers.

sections.heading: What to verify on the listing
paragraphs: Read the model string, then the included pints, then the warranty sentence. NC301, two 16 oz pints included, 7 preset programs, and one year limited are the four lines on this card that a listing has to match. The care line says which parts are dishwasher safe. A return window and a warranty term belong to the maker page or the retailer page you are buying from. This page does not restate a store policy that is not on the maker card.

The recall block below is the catalogue match for the NC301 and for the Foodi 10-in-1. A family name is not the model number. Search NC301 on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts as its own string. Then search the oven’s name as its own string. The dated line under each card is the catalogue check, not a substitute for the model printed on the box.

season.title: AirPods Pro 3 Black Friday: what to know before you buy
season.description: AirPods Pro 3 offer up to 8 hours with noise cancelling, an IP57 rating, and a Hearing Aid feature. The WH-1000XM5 and OpenRun Pro 2 are different headphones, with different play times.
season.subject: airpods-pro-3

sections.heading: AirPods Pro 3 listening lines
paragraphs: The AirPods Pro 3 page states listening of Up to 8 hours with Active Noise Cancellation, transparency of Up to 10 hours with the Hearing Aid feature, a sensor of Heart rate, hearing of Hearing Aid feature, play time of Up to 8 hours with Active Noise Cancellation, and a rating of IP57. A listing that says AirPods, or Pro, still has to match these lines if this is the card you mean. The listening line and the play-time line both say up to 8 hours with Active Noise Cancellation. The transparency line is a different hour count and names the Hearing Aid feature.

The WH-1000XM5 card states battery of Max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on, max. 40 hours with it off, a weight of Approx. 8.82 oz, a charge time of Approx. 3.5 hours, and noise cancelling of 2 processors control 8 microphones. The OpenRun Pro 2 card states play time of Up to 12 hours, a quick charge of 5 minutes for about 150 minutes at 75% volume, and a rating of IP55. One is an over-ear headphone. One is an open-ear headphone. The AirPods card is the in-ear card.

sections.heading: Pick the hour line that matches the form
paragraphs: Pick the AirPods Pro 3 if the listing is that model and you are matching up to 8 hours with Active Noise Cancellation, IP57, and the hearing line that says Hearing Aid feature. The sensor line says heart rate. The transparency line says up to 10 hours with the Hearing Aid feature. Those are Apple’s sentences on this card. A season name in the listing title does not change the model.

Pick the WH-1000XM5 if the listing shows WH-1000XM5 and you are matching max. 30 hours with noise cancelling on, or max. 40 hours with it off, at about 8.82 oz, with a charge time of about 3.5 hours. That is a headband headphone. It is not an in-ear bud, and it does not print IP57. Eight hours and thirty hours are different playback lines.

Pick the OpenRun Pro 2 if the listing is that model and you are matching up to 12 hours, IP55, and the quick-charge sentence of 5 minutes for about 150 minutes at 75% volume. The driver line says dual. That card does not print a noise-cancelling hour line and it does not print IP57. IP55 and IP57 are different rating lines. This page does not treat them as the same code.

sections.heading: What to verify on the listing
paragraphs: Match the generation and the form before the accessory list. AirPods Pro 3 on this card is the listening line of up to 8 hours with Active Noise Cancellation, the IP57 line, and the Hearing Aid feature line. WH-1000XM5 is the over-ear battery line. OpenRun Pro 2 is the open-ear 12 hour line. A case-only listing, or a listing for an earlier Pro generation, is a different card. The comparison with AirPods Pro 2 is the page that lines those two Apple cards up.

The recall block is the catalogue match for each of the three. Confirm the name on the box. Search that name on CPSC Recalls for a US purchase and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts for a Canadian purchase. The dated line on the card is the catalogue check. A listing title is not that check.

season.title: Levoit air purifiers: what to know before you buy
season.description: Core 300S-P, Core 600S-P, and Vital 200S-P are three different purifiers. Noise, cabinet size, and room figures are not the same, and the Classic 300S is a humidifier.
season.subject: levoit-core-300s-p

sections.heading: Three purifier cards, three room sentences
paragraphs: A listing that says Levoit, or 300S, can be more than one card. The Core 300S-P manual states a power supply of AC 120 V, 60 Hz, rated power of 39 W, noise of 22–54.5 dB, dimensions of 8.7 × 8.7 × 14.2 in, and a weight of 7.48 lb. That card does not print a CADR label or a room-size label.

The Core 600S-P page states a room size of 2,909 sq ft at 1 air change per hour, or 606 sq ft at 4.8, noise of 26–55 dB, filtration of 3-stage, CADR of 391 CFM, a weight of 13.7 lb / 6.2 kg, a size of 12.3 x 12.3 x 23.6 in / 31.3 x 31.3 x 60 cm, and power of 49 W, AC 120 V, 60 Hz. The Vital 200S-P page states filtration of 3-stage, a room rate of Changes the air in a 1,862 sq ft room once per hour, noise of As low as 23 dB, a sensor of Infrared dust sensor, and a warranty of 2-year limited. The Classic 300S card in the winter list is a humidifier, with a tank line, not one of these three purifiers.

sections.heading: Pick the cabinet, the CFM line, or the room-rate line
paragraphs: Pick the Core 300S-P if the listing shows that model and you are matching a cabinet of 8.7 × 8.7 × 14.2 in at 7.48 lb, with rated power of 39 W and noise of 22–54.5 dB. Pick it when you do not need a CADR figure from the same page, because this card does not have one. A listing that only says 300S still has to show Core 300S-P if this is the purifier.

Pick the Core 600S-P if you are matching CADR of 391 CFM or the room line 2,909 sq ft at 1 air change per hour, or 606 sq ft at 4.8. The cabinet is 12.3 x 12.3 x 23.6 in / 31.3 x 31.3 x 60 cm at 13.7 lb / 6.2 kg. Power is 49 W, AC 120 V, 60 Hz. Noise is 26–55 dB. The 300S-P noise line is 22–54.5 dB. Those ranges are not the same sentence. The 600S-P page prints both an air-change rate and a CFM figure. Read the sentence you are matching.

Pick the Vital 200S-P if you are matching the room-rate line Changes the air in a 1,862 sq ft room once per hour, filtration of 3-stage, noise of As low as 23 dB, and a sensor line of Infrared dust sensor. The warranty line is 2-year limited. That card does not print a CADR in CFM and it does not print the 300S-P cabinet size. A 1,862 sq ft once-per-hour line is not the 606 sq ft line at 4.8 air changes on the 600S-P page.

sections.heading: What to verify on the listing
paragraphs: Read the full model, not the word Levoit and not the digits 300 alone. Core 300S-P, Core 600S-P, and Vital 200S-P are three purifier strings. Classic 300S is a humidifier card. A filter bundle that names a different model is a different listing. The power line to confirm is 39 W on the 300S-P manual and 49 W on the 600S-P page. The Vital card’s warranty line is 2-year limited. The other two cards on this page do not print that warranty sentence.

The recall block is the catalogue match for each purifier. Search the model on CPSC Recalls and on Health Canada recalls and safety alerts. A season name in the listing is not a CADR figure and it is not the cabinet size. The dated line under the card is the catalogue check. Confirm the name on the rating label before you pay.
